itineraries.destination: Le Marche region, Italy (based around Ripatransone)

items.details: Single villa for all 6 nights; pool with a view, huge common area, 7 bedrooms, marble-island kitchen. Guests settle in on Day 1.
items.name: Private group villa (Le Marche, near Ripatransone)

items.details: Arrival day: Vespa orientation, settle into the villa, wine tasting, Italian dinner by a private chef.
items.name: Vespa orientation and settle in

items.details: Explore medieval hill towns; lunch at their favorite local restaurant; their favorite gelato in Italy; learn to make pasta from scratch.
items.name: Medieval Hill Towns exploration

items.details: Lunch stop on the hill-towns day; the specific restaurant is unnamed in the source.
items.name: Favorite local restaurant (lunch)

items.details: Drive Vespa to the beach; swim in the Adriatic Sea; seafood lunch; back to the beach (or the villa); outdoor dinner in a beautiful medieval hill town.
items.name: Beach Day

items.details: Seafood lunch during beach day; specific place not named in the source.
items.name: Seafood lunch (Adriatic coast)

items.details: Tour and tasting at a local cheese factory; tasting (and possibly a tour) at a local prosciutto factory; dinner at an incredibly beautiful local winery.
items.name: Local Delicacies day

items.details: Dinner at an incredibly beautiful local winery; winery not named in the source.
items.name: Winery dinner

items.details: Day was still TBD in the itinerary at time of writing; a winery tour will probably be involved.
items.name: Day 5 - TBD (winery tour likely)

items.details: Free day to do what you enjoyed most; 'the world's best pizza party'; learn to make pizza from scratch in a wood-burning oven.
items.name: Pizza Party day

items.details: Part with the Vespa; group transport back to the train station/airport and goodbye.
items.name: Departure: return Vespa, transfer to train station/airport

itineraries.summary: A hosted 7-day / 6-night group Vespa tour through the Le Marche countryside (based on Kara and Nate's own 10 days in Ripatransone). Guests stay in one private villa with pool, 7 bedrooms, marble-island kitchen; days are suggestion-style with open afternoons. Published trip cost was $2,800 per person (flights not included), covering accommodations, every meal, unlimited local wine at the villa, Vespa + insurance + helmets. Registration sold out for three trips.
itineraries.title: Italy Vespa Tour (Le Marche, Italy)

itineraries.destination: Moscow to Vladivostok, via Irkutsk and Ulan-Ude

items.details: 74 hours of non-stop train travel; first leg of the journey. Source also covers visa process, ticket buying, and train-class choices.
items.name: Trans-Siberian train: Moscow to Irkutsk

items.details: Stopped in Irkutsk for two nights. Main draw is Lake Baikal, the deepest lake in the world; Olkhon Island is the popular overnight island (ferry), but needs at least 3 days total (7h travel each leg), which they wish they'd scheduled.
items.name: Irkutsk - Lake Baikal (Olkhon Island)

items.details: Short 6.5 hour ride to the second stop, Ulan-Ude.
items.name: Train: Irkutsk to Ulan-Ude

items.details: Stayed two nights, but they say one day is enough: world's largest statue of Lenin's head, main walking street, a church near the end of the walking street, a monastery on a hill overlooking the city, and another monastery 45 minutes outside the city.
items.name: Ulan-Ude sightseeing

items.details: Final leg: another 64 hours of non-stop train travel to Vladivostok. They found no interesting stops between Ulan-Ude and Vladivostok.
items.name: Train: Ulan-Ude to Vladivostok

items.details: End of the railway journey; they note their Vladivostok time was cut short by their onward flight needs and would have spent more time there.
items.name: Vladivostok stopover

items.details: Three-step visa process for US passport holders: letter of invitation (they got one via Fortuna Travel for $12 after VisaHQ quoted $50/person for the letter), visa application (delivered in person to a Russian consulate or via visa service), and visa registration within 7 working days in Russia.
items.name: Russian visa logistics (pre-trip)

items.details: Locals in Moscow recommended stopping in Kazan (predominantly Muslim city); they also recommend booking a stop in Yekaterinburg (where the last tsar was executed) for those interested in Russian history.
items.name: Suggested additional stops: Kazan and Yekaterinburg

itineraries.summary: Kara and Nate's own 11-day (they state '10 days and 11 nights' in the route section) Trans-Siberian journey covering 9,280 km: Moscow to Irkutsk (74h non-stop train), 2 nights Irkutsk (Lake Baikal gateway), 6.5h train to Ulan-Ude, 2 nights Ulan-Ude, then 64h non-stop train to Vladivostok. 7 nights slept on the train, 2 nights in a hostel, 2 nights in a hotel. The post is a full practical guide (Russian visa steps, route choice, ticket buying) plus what they'd do differently. Day numbering here is approximate (derived from leg durations in the source) - the post is leg-structured, not day-numbered.
itineraries.title: The Ultimate Guide to Riding the Trans-Siberian Railway (Moscow to Vladivostok)

notes: Two genuine itineraries extracted from karaandnate.com blog posts (their own content, no paywall). (1) Italy Vespa Tour: explicit 7-day group tour itinerary with pricing ($2,800/person, flights excluded); high confidence day-by-day. (2) Trans-Siberian Railway guide: their 11-day Moscow-to-Vladivostok journey with leg-by-leg route, durations, and practical tips; day numbers are approximate since the source is leg-structured, not day-numbered (medium confidence). No hotel/restaurant names were given for either trip, so those are left generic rather than invented. Booking links omitted (sold-out registration links had no usable URLs).
